        From a8cabc612b16834260831a8163ae4b479b5c33a5 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Yu Watanabe <watanabe.yu+github@gmail.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Oct 2017 12:27:13 +0900
Subject: [PATCH] core: fix segfault in compile_bind_mounts() when BindPaths=
 or BindReadOnlyPaths= is set

This fixes a bug introduced by 6c47cd7d3bf35c8158a0737f34fe2c5dc95e72d6.

Fixes #7055.
---
 src/core/execute.c | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/src/core/execute.c b/src/core/execute.c
index d7d2ce4947..e64afe8e9c 100644
--- a/src/core/execute.c
+++ b/src/core/execute.c
@@ -2161,7 +2161,7 @@ static int compile_bind_mounts(
         if (!bind_mounts)
                 return -ENOMEM;
 
-        for (i = 0; context->n_bind_mounts; i++) {
+        for (i = 0; i < context->n_bind_mounts; i++) {
                 BindMount *item = context->bind_mounts + i;
                 char *s, *d;
 
--

        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by an incorrect loop condition in the `compile_bind_mounts()` function. The original code used `for (i = 0; context->n_bind_mounts; i++)`, which would lead to an infinite loop if `context->n_bind_mounts` was non-zero, as it does not properly check the loop index against the number of bind mounts. This could result in accessing out-of-bounds memory, leading to a segmentation fault. The fix changes the loop condition to `for (i = 0; i < context->n_bind_mounts; i++)`, ensuring that the loop iterates only over valid indices of the `bind_mounts` array.

Root cause:
The bug was caused by an incorrect loop condition in the `compile_bind_mounts()` function. The original code used `for (i = 0; context->n_bind_mounts; i++)`, which would lead to an infinite loop if `context->n_bind_mounts` was non-zero, as it does not properly check the loop index against the number of bind mounts. This could result in accessing out-of-bounds memory, leading to a segmentation fault. The fix changes the loop condition to `for (i = 0; i < context->n_bind_mounts; i++)`, ensuring that the loop iterates only over valid indices of the `bind_mounts` array.
